# Gelabber v0.8.2

Integrated through the PRs #383 to #390 and #392 into `v0.8` and the version
PR into `main`.

**Operators: update media together with web, or media first.** The web
client now sends video in three layers, which the v0.8.1 media server
refuses: a v0.8.2 web client against it cannot publish camera or screen
video. The Compose pins move together, so pulling and restarting the stack
is enough. No database migration, no `.env`, `compose.yaml` or `Caddyfile`
changes beyond the image pins.

## Video quality (#392)

A 4K share from the desktop app reached viewers at 540p. Now:

- **Viewers start on the best layer.** The media server's own estimate steps
  a viewer down only when their connection needs it. The size of the tile no
  longer picks the layer.
- **Bitrate follows the picture.** Each layer may use up to
  width × height × fps × 0.1 bit/s, about 6 Mbit/s at 1080p30 and 50 Mbit/s
  at 4K60, instead of libwebrtc's default of 5 Mbit/s at most. The sender
  starts its estimate at 5 Mbit/s, the server at 8 Mbit/s. An upload limit
  or economy mode still applies and is split across the layers by these
  ceilings.
- **Three layers.** VP8 and H.264 send full, half and quarter size instead
  of two layers.
- **Codecs.** The order is AV1 with hardware encoding, H.264 with hardware
  encoding, VP8, H.264, VP9, AV1. A browser counts as able to receive AV1
  when it decodes 4K smoothly, so Firefox no longer removes AV1 from the
  room. VP9 in three spatial layers (`L3T3_KEY`) is used only in rooms that
  lack VP8 and H.264.
- **Diagnostics** show which codec was picked and why.

## Desktop app

- **Update notice.** A desktop app older than the web UI, or one that
  reports no version, shows a notice once per page. Apps from v0.6 and v0.7
  report neither hardware H.264 nor hardware AV1, so the web client sent
  VP8 from them.
- The app reports VP9 in spatial layers (`vp9-svc`) and gets 10 s instead of
  1 s to answer the codec probe; a probe that timed out is asked again.

## Interface

- **Inter** (#387). The interface is set in Inter, served by Gelabber
  itself (105 kB; the extended Latin and italic files load only when text
  needs them). The licence is served as `/inter-license.txt`.
- **Avatars** (#385). Initials sit on a tint picked by the name, so a person
  keeps one colour on every screen.
- **Server rail** (#388). A pill at the rail's edge marks the active server,
  tiles are round at rest, and mentions keep their red count.
- **Emoji picker** (#384) leaves out emoji this device cannot draw instead of
  showing empty boxes.
- **Long press on touch screens** (#389, #390). Channel and category actions
  and the notification settings of server tiles, the DM tile and
  conversation rows open from a held finger, now also on iOS. The "…" on
  every row is gone; keyboards and screen readers still reach it.
- **Smaller fixes** (#383, #386). Toasts sit above the call dock on desktop
  too. Theme cards keep visible borders in dark themes. The live spotlight
  takes at most half the window and 520 px. Hidden row actions no longer cut
  channel names short. Offline members are dimmed. The composer has the
  stronger field border.

## Upgrade notes

- Image pins `GELABBER_{API,WEB,MEDIA}_IMAGE` move together to `v0.8.2`. If
  you set them yourself, move media first or together with web, never web
  alone. A v0.8.1 web client works with the v0.8.2 media server.
- Expect more outgoing traffic from the media server: every viewer now
  starts on the top layer, small tiles included.
- Rollback: the v0.8.1 image set, all three together. The database is
  unchanged.
- **Desktop, Windows:** the installer and `latest.json` are attached to this
  release; older apps offer the update.
- **Desktop, Linux (Arch):** update from the pacman repository.

## Open

- **AV1 is one stream.** Every viewer gets the full picture; a viewer with
  less download stutters instead of stepping down. This is being tested in
  a real call. If viewers stutter, a follow-up moves hardware H.264 (three
  layers) ahead of AV1.
- The receive-loss scenario in `web/scripts/e2e/mediasoup-native.mjs` has
  not run against a live stack yet.
